connectors.name: Azure DevOps
connectors.description: Trigger workflows from the work items a WIQL query returns.
connectors.auth: Signs in with your Azure identity — `az login` is usually all it needs.

triggers.label: Work item matches the query
triggers.description: Fires once per work item the WIQL query newly returns.

actions.label: Create a work item
actions.description: Add a work item to the board and return its id and url.

actions.label: Update a work item
actions.description: Change the title, state, description or assignee of a work item.

env.name: ADO_ORGANIZATION
env.description: Name or URL, e.g. "contoso" or https://dev.azure.com/contoso

env.name: ADO_QUERY
env.description: Work items to poll, e.g. SELECT [System.Id] FROM WorkItems WHERE [System.State] = 'New' ORDER BY [System.ChangedDate] DESC

env.name: ADO_TOP
env.description: Upper bound on work items read in one poll.

connectors.name: Airtable
connectors.description: Trigger workflows from new or updated Airtable records, and create, update, upsert, delete or read records and base schemas from a step.
connectors.auth: Paste an Airtable personal access token with data.records:read, data.records:write and schema.bases:read, granted access to the bases it should reach. There is no Airtable CLI to sign in with.

triggers.label: A record is created
triggers.description: Fires once for each record created in the table since the last poll, oldest first.

triggers.label: A record is updated
triggers.description: Fires for each record modified since the last poll. Name a last-modified-time field to stamp items with the real time; without one the poll time stands in.

actions.label: Create a record
actions.description: Add one record to a table.

actions.label: Update a record
actions.description: Change the given fields of a record and leave the rest as they were.

actions.label: Upsert records
actions.description: Create or update up to 10 records at once, matching each on the merge fields: no match creates, one match updates, several fail the call.

actions.label: Delete a record
actions.description: Delete one record. A second call for the same id answers 404.

actions.label: Get a record
actions.description: Read one record by id. Empty cells are omitted from fields.

actions.label: List records
actions.description: List the records of a table, optionally filtered by a formula or a view, up to maxRecords across pages.

actions.label: List bases
actions.description: The bases the token can reach, 1000 at a time, with the permission level it holds on each.

actions.label: Get a base schema
actions.description: The tables of a base with their fields and views.

env.name: AIRTABLE_API_KEY
env.description: A personal access token from airtable.com/create/tokens with the scopes data.records:read, data.records:write and schema.bases:read, granted access to each base it should reach.

env.name: AIRTABLE_BASE_ID
env.description: The base the triggers watch, app… from the base URL or listBases.

env.name: AIRTABLE_TABLE
env.description: The table the triggers watch, by id (tbl…) or by name.

env.name: AIRTABLE_VIEW
env.description: A view name or id to watch. Records hidden by the view are skipped. Blank for the whole table.

env.name: AIRTABLE_FILTER_BY_FORMULA
env.description: An extra Airtable formula a record must satisfy, such as {Status} = "Open".

env.name: AIRTABLE_LAST_MODIFIED_FIELD
env.description: The name of a "Last modified time" field in the table, for the updated-record trigger. Blank falls back to LAST_MODIFIED_TIME() and the poll time.

connectors.name: Anthropic
connectors.description: Trigger workflows when a message batch finishes or a model becomes available, and create messages, count tokens, list models and run message batches from a step.
connectors.auth: Paste an Anthropic API key from console.anthropic.com/settings/keys for a single workspace. There is no CLI to sign in with.

triggers.label: A message batch finished
triggers.description: Fires once for each message batch whose processing has ended since the last poll, oldest first. Read the results with getBatchResults.

triggers.label: A model became available
triggers.description: Fires once for each model released since the last poll, oldest first. The first poll looks 30 days back.

actions.label: Create a message
actions.description: Send a conversation to a model and get its reply. Every call bills a generation.

actions.label: Count tokens
actions.description: Count the tokens a conversation and system prompt would use, without creating a message.

actions.label: List models
actions.description: The models the key can use, newest release first.

actions.label: Get a model
actions.description: Read one model by id, or resolve an alias to its model id.

actions.label: Create a message batch
actions.description: Queue up to 100,000 message requests for asynchronous processing. Two calls queue two batches.

actions.label: Get a message batch
actions.description: Read a batch and its request counts; poll it until processingStatus is ended.

actions.label: Get batch results
actions.description: Read the results of an ended batch, one entry per request, matched by custom_id rather than by order.

actions.label: Cancel a message batch
actions.description: Ask for a batch to stop; it enters canceling and requests already running may still finish.

env.name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
env.description: An API key from console.anthropic.com/settings/keys, for a single workspace.

connectors.name: Discord
connectors.description: Trigger workflows from new Discord messages, members and threads, and send messages, reply in threads, react, pin or read channels and members from a step.
connectors.auth: Paste a bot token from the Developer Portal (Bot tab, Reset Token). There is no Discord CLI to sign in with.

triggers.label: A message is posted in a channel
triggers.description: Fires once per new message in the channel or thread. Bot and system messages are skipped unless the connection includes them. Reading the text needs the Message Content intent.

triggers.label: A member joins the server
triggers.description: Fires once per member who joined the guild since the last poll. Needs the Server Members intent.

triggers.label: A thread is created
triggers.description: Fires once per active thread created since the last poll, in every channel of the guild or only under the configured channel.

actions.label: Send a message
actions.description: Post a message to a channel or thread, optionally as a reply and with embeds.

actions.label: Reply in a thread
actions.description: Start a thread from a message, or use the one it already has, and post a reply in it.

actions.label: Add a reaction
actions.description: React to a message with a Unicode or custom emoji.

actions.label: Pin a message
actions.description: Pin a message in its channel. Pinning one already pinned is a no-op.

actions.label: List channels
actions.description: The channels of a guild, sorted by position. Threads are not included.

actions.label: Get a channel
actions.description: Read one channel or thread by id.

actions.label: Get a server member
actions.description: Read one member of a guild, with their nickname, roles and join date.

env.name: DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN
env.description: From https://discord.com/developers/applications: open the application, Bot tab, Reset Token, and paste the token it shows once. Sent as `Authorization: Bot <token>`.

env.name: DISCORD_CHANNEL_ID
env.description: Channel or thread id (Developer Mode → right-click → Copy Channel ID). Required by the message trigger; narrows the thread trigger to one parent channel.

env.name: DISCORD_GUILD_ID
env.description: Guild (server) id. Required by the member and thread triggers.

env.name: DISCORD_INCLUDE_BOTS
env.description: Deliver messages whose author is a bot, including this one’s. Off by default so a workflow that posts into the channel it watches does not loop.

env.name: DISCORD_INCLUDE_SYSTEM
env.description: Deliver joins, pins, boosts, thread notices and other messages nobody typed.

env.name: DISCORD_LOOKBACK_MINUTES
env.description: How far back the very first poll looks. Later polls continue from where the last one stopped.

env.name: DISCORD_MAX_PAGES
env.description: Pages of 100 messages or 1000 members one poll walks before leaving the rest for the next.

connectors.name: GitHub
connectors.description: Trigger workflows from GitHub issues and pull requests, and open, close or comment on them from a step.
connectors.auth: Borrows the GitHub CLI's login — `gh auth login` is all it needs, and no token is stored here.

triggers.label: An issue is created
triggers.description: Fires for each issue opened since the last poll.

triggers.label: A pull request is opened
triggers.description: Fires for each pull request opened since the last poll.

actions.label: Create an issue
actions.description: Open a new issue in the connected repository.

actions.label: Close an issue
actions.description: Close an issue or pull request in the connected repository.

actions.label: Comment on an issue
actions.description: Post a comment on an issue or pull request.

actions.label: Open a pull request
actions.description: Open a pull request from a pushed branch into the base branch.

env.name: GITHUB_OWNER
env.description: User or organisation, e.g. vorn-run

env.name: GITHUB_REPO
env.description: Repository name on its own, without the owner

env.name: GITHUB_LABELS
env.description: Comma-separated. Applies to the issue trigger only.

connectors.name: GitLab
connectors.description: Trigger workflows from GitLab issues, merge requests and pipeline results, and create or comment on issues and merge requests from a step.
connectors.auth: Borrows the GitLab CLI's login — `glab auth login` is all it needs — or takes a personal access token if you would rather paste one.

triggers.label: An issue is created
triggers.description: Fires once for each issue created in the project since the last poll.

triggers.label: A merge request is opened
triggers.description: Fires once for each merge request opened in the project since the last poll.

triggers.label: A pipeline finishes
triggers.description: Fires once for each pipeline that reaches success, failed, canceled or skipped, with the status on the item.

actions.label: Create an issue
actions.description: Open a new issue in a project.

actions.label: Comment on an issue
actions.description: Post a note on an issue.

actions.label: Comment on a merge request
actions.description: Post a note on a merge request.

actions.label: Get a project
actions.description: Read a project by path or id.

actions.label: List open merge requests
actions.description: The open merge requests of a project, most recently updated first.

actions.label: Get an issue
actions.description: Read one issue by its number.

env.name: GITLAB_BASE_URL
env.description: Instance URL without a trailing slash. Leave the default for gitlab.com.

env.name: GITLAB_PROJECT
env.description: Path such as group/project, or the numeric id. The triggers poll this project.

env.name: GITLAB_TOKEN
env.description: Leave empty to borrow the glab CLI login. Needs scope api, or read_api for the triggers and read-only actions.

env.name: GITLAB_REF
env.description: Branch or tag whose pipelines to watch. Blank for every ref.

connectors.name: HubSpot
connectors.description: Trigger workflows from new HubSpot contacts, companies and deals or deal stage changes, and create, update, search, annotate or associate CRM records from a step.
connectors.auth: Paste a HubSpot private app access token with the contacts, companies and deals read and write scopes, crm.objects.owners.read and crm.schemas.deals.read. There is no HubSpot CLI to borrow a CRM login from.

triggers.label: A contact is created
triggers.description: Fires once for each contact created since the last poll, oldest first.

triggers.label: A deal is created
triggers.description: Fires once for each deal created since the last poll, oldest first, in the configured pipeline or in all of them.

triggers.label: A company is created
triggers.description: Fires once for each company created since the last poll, oldest first.

triggers.label: A deal moves to a stage
triggers.description: Fires once per deal and stage when a deal is found at a stage it has not fired for; a deal edited without changing stage is dropped. Filter by pipeline and stage in the settings.

actions.label: Create a contact
actions.description: Add a contact by email. An email that already exists answers 409 with the existing id in the message.

actions.label: Update a contact
actions.description: Set the given properties of a contact and leave the rest as they were.

actions.label: Create a deal
actions.description: Add a deal at a stage of a pipeline. Every call makes a new deal.

actions.label: Update a deal
actions.description: Set the given properties of a deal, such as {"dealstage":"closedwon"}, and leave the rest as they were.

actions.label: Create a company
actions.description: Add a company by name, with its domain when known. Every call makes a new company.

actions.label: Add a note to a record
actions.description: Attach a note to a contact, company or deal, stamped with the current time.

actions.label: Associate two records
actions.description: Link two records with the default association for their types, or with a labelled type id.

actions.label: Get a contact
actions.description: Read one contact by record id or by email address.

actions.label: Search contacts
actions.description: Find contacts by free text or by filter groups, one page at a time.

actions.label: List deal pipelines
actions.description: The deal pipelines of the account with their stages.

actions.label: List owners
actions.description: The users who can own records, with the id to assign a record by.

env.name: HUBSPOT_ACCESS_TOKEN
env.description: The access token of a private app from Settings, Integrations, Private Apps, with the crm.objects.contacts, crm.objects.companies and crm.objects.deals read and write scopes, crm.objects.owners.read and crm.schemas.deals.read.

env.name: HUBSPOT_PORTAL_ID
env.description: The account number in the app.hubspot.com URL, used to give each item a link to open the record. Blank leaves items without a URL.

env.name: HUBSPOT_PROPERTIES
env.description: Comma-separated internal property names every trigger fetches on top of the standard set.

env.name: HUBSPOT_PIPELINE
env.description: A pipeline id from listDealPipelines; the deal triggers then watch only that pipeline. Blank watches every pipeline.

env.name: HUBSPOT_DEAL_STAGE
env.description: A stage id such as closedwon or a numeric custom stage id; the stage-changed trigger then fires only for deals reaching it.

connectors.name: Jira
connectors.description: Trigger workflows when a Jira Cloud issue is created, updated or moved to a status, and create, edit, transition, comment on, assign, read or search issues from a step.
connectors.auth: Paste your Atlassian site URL, account email and an API token from id.atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens. There is no Jira CLI to sign in with.

triggers.label: An issue is created
triggers.description: Fires once for each issue created since the last poll, oldest first, within the project and JQL filter from the settings.

triggers.label: An issue is updated
triggers.description: Fires for each change to an issue since the last poll, keyed by issue and update time, so an issue edited twice fires twice.

triggers.label: An issue moves to a status
triggers.description: Fires when an issue is transitioned into the status named in the settings. JQL records that the change happened, not when, so the issue's last update stands in as the time.

actions.label: Create an issue
actions.description: Create one issue in a project. The description is written as plain text and converted to Atlassian Document Format.

actions.label: Update an issue
actions.description: Edit the summary, description or any fields of an issue; the rest stays as it was. Transitions are ignored here, use transitionIssue.

actions.label: Transition an issue
actions.description: Move an issue through a workflow transition, by transition id or name, optionally with a comment and screen fields.

actions.label: Add a comment
actions.description: Post a comment on an issue. Plain text is converted to Atlassian Document Format.

actions.label: Assign an issue
actions.description: Assign an issue to an account, or unassign it.

actions.label: Get an issue
actions.description: Read one issue by key or id, with its main fields flattened and the description as plain text.

actions.label: Search issues
actions.description: Run a JQL query and return the matching issues, paging until maxResults are collected.

actions.label: List transitions
actions.description: The workflow transitions an issue can take from its current status.

actions.label: List projects
actions.description: The projects the account can browse, ordered by key, optionally filtered by a name or key fragment and by type.

actions.label: Get the current user
actions.description: The account the API token belongs to, with its account id and time zone.

env.name: JIRA_SITE_URL
env.description: Your Jira Cloud site, such as https://example.atlassian.net.

env.name: JIRA_EMAIL
env.description: The email address of the Atlassian account the API token belongs to.

env.name: JIRA_API_TOKEN
env.description: An API token from https://id.atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens, created without scopes. Every issue created or comment posted is attributed to this account.

env.name: JIRA_PROJECT_KEY
env.description: Limit the triggers to one project, by key (EX). Blank watches every project the account can browse.

env.name: JIRA_JQL
env.description: An extra JQL filter every trigger applies, such as issuetype = Bug AND priority in (High, Highest).

env.name: JIRA_STATUS
env.description: The status name the issueTransitioned trigger watches for, such as Done. Only that trigger reads it.

connectors.name: Azure Data Explorer
connectors.description: Trigger workflows from the rows a KQL query returns.
connectors.auth: Signs in with your Azure identity — `az login` is usually all it needs.

triggers.label: Query returns a row
triggers.description: Fires once per new row returned by the configured KQL query.

actions.label: Run a KQL query
actions.description: Run a read-only query and return its rows.

env.name: KUSTO_CLUSTER
env.description: Cluster name or URL, e.g. "help" or https://help.kusto.windows.net

env.name: KUSTO_QUERY
env.description: Query to poll. Reference vorn_since and vorn_limit to bound it.

env.name: KUSTO_ID_COLUMN
env.description: Column holding a stable per-row id. Vorn dedupes on it.

env.name: KUSTO_TIMESTAMP_COLUMN
env.description: Column the poll watermark advances from.

env.name: KUSTO_LOOKBACK
env.description: How far back the very first poll looks, e.g. 30m, 2h, 7d.

connectors.name: Linear
connectors.description: Trigger workflows from Linear issues, and comment or close them from a step.
connectors.auth: Uses a Linear personal API key, created at linear.app/settings/api.

triggers.label: An issue is created or changed
triggers.description: Fires for each issue the query returns that Vorn has not seen at this time.

actions.label: Comment on an issue
actions.description: Post a comment on a Linear issue.

actions.label: Create an issue
actions.description: Open a new Linear issue and return its identifier and url.

actions.label: Close an issue
actions.description: Move an issue to the first completed state its team defines.

env.name: LINEAR_API_KEY
env.description: Create a personal API key at linear.app/settings/api.

env.name: LINEAR_TEAM_KEY
env.description: Upper-case key such as ENG. Leave blank for every team you can see.

env.name: LINEAR_STATE_TYPE
env.description: One of backlog, unstarted, started, completed, canceled. Blank for all states.

connectors.name: MySQL
connectors.description: Trigger workflows from new or updated rows in a MySQL or MariaDB database, and query or write to it from a step.
connectors.auth: Paste the database's connection URL (mysql://user:password@host:3306/database) from your provider's dashboard or your DBA; SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE on the tables the workflow touches, as the steps demand, is enough.

triggers.label: New rows in a table
triggers.description: Fires once per row inserted after the last seen value of the ordering column.

triggers.label: Updated rows in a table
triggers.description: Fires once per change to a row, tracked by its updated_at column and primary key.

actions.label: Run a query
actions.description: Run one SQL statement with positional parameters; returns rows for a read and the counts for a write.

actions.label: Select rows
actions.description: Read rows from a table, with an optional parameterised WHERE.

actions.label: Insert a row
actions.description: Insert one row and return its AUTO_INCREMENT id.

actions.label: Update rows
actions.description: Set columns on the rows a WHERE matches and return how many matched.

actions.label: Delete rows
actions.description: Delete the rows a WHERE matches and return how many went.

actions.label: List tables
actions.description: List the tables and views in a database that the user can see.

actions.label: Describe a table
actions.description: List the columns of a table with their types, nullability, keys and defaults.

actions.label: Count rows
actions.description: Count the rows in a table, optionally those a WHERE matches.

env.name: MYSQL_URL
env.description: mysql://user:password@host:3306/database. Your provider shows it on the database page; otherwise ask your DBA. The user needs SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE on the tables the workflow touches, as the steps demand.

env.name: MYSQL_SSL
env.description: One of disabled, required, verify-full. Default disabled. "required" encrypts without checking the certificate, which the driver strongly discourages; "verify-full" checks the chain and host name.

env.name: MYSQL_SSL_CA
env.description: Path to a PEM CA bundle for verify-full against a private CA. Blank uses Node's roots.

env.name: MYSQL_TABLE
env.description: For both triggers: table or db.table to watch.

env.name: MYSQL_ORDERING_COLUMN
env.description: For "new rows": a column that only grows, such as an AUTO_INCREMENT id or created_at.

env.name: MYSQL_KEY_COLUMN
env.description: The primary key column. Defaults to the ordering column for "new rows"; required for "updated rows".

env.name: MYSQL_UPDATED_AT_COLUMN
env.description: For "updated rows": a DATETIME or TIMESTAMP column, ideally ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP.

env.name: MYSQL_WHERE
env.description: Optional SQL placed after WHERE to narrow the rows a trigger watches, e.g. status = 'open'. No placeholders.

env.name: MYSQL_START_FROM
env.description: Value of the ordering column to start after ("new rows") or of updated_at to start at ("updated rows"). Blank means the newest page.

env.name: MYSQL_TITLE_COLUMN
env.description: Column to use as the item title. Blank uses the table and key.

env.name: MYSQL_LIMIT
env.description: Default 100, at most 1000.

connectors.name: Notion
connectors.description: Trigger workflows from Notion database pages, and create or update them.
connectors.auth: Paste a Notion integration token, then share the pages you want it to see with the connection in Notion. There is no Notion CLI to sign in with.

triggers.label: A page is created or changed
triggers.description: Fires once per page in the database that Vorn has not seen at this time. Deleted and moved pages produce no event — polling only sees what still matches.

actions.label: Create a page
actions.description: Add a page to the configured data source.

actions.label: Update a page
actions.description: Set properties on an existing page.

actions.label: Find pages
actions.description: Query the configured data source and return the pages it matches.

env.name: NOTION_TOKEN
env.description: An internal integration token or personal API key from notion.so/profile/integrations. There is no Notion CLI to sign in with.

env.name: NOTION_DATABASE_ID
env.description: Paste the database URL, or the 32-character id from it.

env.name: NOTION_DATA_SOURCE_ID
env.description: Only needed when the database has more than one data source. Blank resolves it.

env.name: NOTION_FILTER
env.description: A JSON filter in Notion's own syntax, ANDed with the poll watermark.

env.name: NOTION_STATUS_PROPERTY
env.description: Name of the property carrying status. Blank uses the first status, then select, property.

connectors.name: OpenAI
connectors.description: Trigger workflows when an OpenAI batch or fine-tuning job finishes or a file is uploaded, and create responses, chat completions, embeddings, moderations and batches from a step.
connectors.auth: Paste an API key from https://platform.openai.com/api-keys. There is no OpenAI CLI to sign in with.

triggers.label: A batch finishes
triggers.description: Fires once when a batch reaches completed, failed, expired or cancelled. The list has no status filter, so every batch created inside the look-back is read and the terminal ones kept.

triggers.label: A file is uploaded
triggers.description: Fires once per file uploaded since the last poll, newest first from GET /files.

triggers.label: A fine-tuning job finishes
triggers.description: Fires once when a fine-tuning job reaches succeeded, failed or cancelled.

actions.label: Create a response
actions.description: Ask a model for a response with the Responses API, optionally constrained to a JSON schema. Spends tokens; not stored unless asked.

actions.label: Create a chat completion
actions.description: Ask a model for the next message in a conversation with the Chat Completions API. Spends tokens.

actions.label: Create embeddings
actions.description: Turn text into embedding vectors. The same input yields the same vectors and nothing is stored.

actions.label: Moderate text
actions.description: Classify text against OpenAI’s usage policies. Free, and nothing is stored.

actions.label: List models
actions.description: List the models the key can use, with their owner.

actions.label: Get a model
actions.description: Read one model by id. An unknown id answers 404 model_not_found.

actions.label: List files
actions.description: List uploaded files, newest first, optionally by purpose.

actions.label: Get a batch
actions.description: Read one batch by id, with its status, request counts and output files.

actions.label: Create a batch
actions.description: Queue a batch of requests from an uploaded JSONL file. Each call queues a new batch that runs and bills.

env.name: OPENAI_API_KEY
env.description: Sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Create one at https://platform.openai.com/api-keys (Create new secret key) and set OPENAI_API_KEY on the connection.

env.name: OPENAI_ORGANIZATION
env.description: Organization id (org-…), sent as OpenAI-Organization. Only needed when the key belongs to more than one organization.

env.name: OPENAI_PROJECT
env.description: Project id (proj_…), sent as OpenAI-Project. Only needed when a legacy user key should bill one project.

env.name: OPENAI_BATCH_ENDPOINT
env.description: Only batches for this endpoint, such as /v1/chat/completions. Empty delivers every batch.

env.name: OPENAI_BATCH_LOOKBACK_HOURS
env.description: How far before the watermark the batch poll reads, because a batch finishes up to a day after it is created.

env.name: OPENAI_FILE_PURPOSE
env.description: Only files uploaded with this purpose (assistants, assistants_output, batch, batch_output, fine-tune, fine-tune-results, vision, user_data). Empty delivers every file.

env.name: OPENAI_FINE_TUNING_LOOKBACK_HOURS
env.description: How far before the watermark the fine-tuning poll reads, because a job is created long before it finishes.

connectors.name: PostgreSQL
connectors.description: Trigger workflows from new rows in a PostgreSQL database, and query or write to it from a step.
connectors.auth: Paste the database's connection string (postgres://user:password@host:5432/db?sslmode=require) from your provider's dashboard or your DBA; a read-only role is enough for triggers.

triggers.label: New rows in a table
triggers.description: Fires once per row inserted after the last seen value of the ordering column.

triggers.label: Rows matching a query
triggers.description: Fires once per row your SELECT returns beyond the cursor value it was last run with.

actions.label: Run a query
actions.description: Run SQL text with positional parameters and return its rows and row count.

actions.label: Select rows
actions.description: Read rows from a table, with an optional parameterised WHERE.

actions.label: Insert a row
actions.description: Insert one row and return it as stored.

actions.label: Update rows
actions.description: Set columns on the rows a WHERE matches and return how many changed.

actions.label: List tables
actions.description: List the tables and views in a schema that the role can see.

actions.label: Describe a table
actions.description: List the columns of a table with their types and nullability.

env.name: DATABASE_URL
env.description: libpq URI: postgres://user:password@host:5432/database?sslmode=require. Your provider shows it on the database page; otherwise ask your DBA. A read-only role is enough for triggers.

env.name: PG_TABLE
env.description: For "new rows": table or schema.table to watch.

env.name: PG_ORDERING_COLUMN
env.description: For "new rows": a column that only grows, such as id or created_at.

env.name: PG_KEY_COLUMN
env.description: The column that identifies a row, usually the primary key. Defaults to the ordering column for "new rows"; required for "rows matching a query".

env.name: PG_QUERY
env.description: For "rows matching a query": a SELECT with $1 where the cursor goes and, optionally, $2 for the limit, ordered by the cursor column ascending.

env.name: PG_CURSOR_COLUMN
env.description: For "rows matching a query": the result column the cursor advances from.

env.name: PG_START_FROM
env.description: Value of the ordering or cursor column to start after. Required for "rows matching a query"; for "new rows", blank means the newest page.

env.name: PG_TITLE_COLUMN
env.description: Column to use as the item title. Blank uses the table and key.

connectors.name: Slack
connectors.description: Trigger workflows from Slack messages, thread replies and channel members, and post, reply or react from a step.
connectors.auth: Uses a bot token from a Slack app installed to the workspace: api.slack.com/apps, OAuth & Permissions, Bot User OAuth Token.

triggers.label: A message is posted in a channel
triggers.description: Fires for each new message in the configured channel. Bot and system messages are skipped unless includeBots is true.

triggers.label: A reply is posted in a thread
triggers.description: Fires for each new reply under the configured parent message.

triggers.label: A member joins a channel
triggers.description: Fires once for each user id in the channel that has not been seen before.

actions.label: Post a message
actions.description: Post a message to a channel, optionally under a thread or with Block Kit blocks.

actions.label: Reply in a thread
actions.description: Post a reply under a parent message.

actions.label: Add a reaction
actions.description: React to a message with an emoji.

actions.label: List channels
actions.description: List the public and private channels the bot can see, unarchived only.

actions.label: Get a channel
actions.description: Read one channel by id.

actions.label: Find a user by email
actions.description: Look a user up by the address registered on the workspace.

actions.label: Get a user
actions.description: Read one user by id.

env.name: SLACK_BOT_TOKEN
env.description: Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-…) of a Slack app installed to the workspace, from api.slack.com/apps under OAuth & Permissions.

env.name: SLACK_CHANNEL
env.description: Channel id such as C0123456789 the triggers watch. The bot must be a member.

env.name: SLACK_THREAD_TS
env.description: The parent message ts, such as 1512085950.000216, for the reply trigger.

env.name: SLACK_INCLUDE_BOTS
env.description: true delivers messages with a subtype or a bot_id too; joins, topic changes, app posts.

env.name: SLACK_LIMIT
env.description: Messages read per request, 1 to 999.

connectors.name: Stripe
connectors.description: Trigger workflows from new Stripe customers, succeeded payments and paid or failed invoices, and create customers, issue refunds or read balances and charges from a step.
connectors.auth: Borrows the Stripe CLI's login — `stripe login` is all it needs — or takes a restricted or secret API key if you would rather paste one.

triggers.label: A customer is created
triggers.description: Fires once for each customer created since the last poll.

triggers.label: A payment succeeds
triggers.description: Fires once for each payment intent that reaches succeeded. Amounts are integers in the smallest currency unit.

triggers.label: An invoice is paid
triggers.description: Fires once for each invoice that becomes paid, stamped with when it was paid.

triggers.label: An invoice payment fails
triggers.description: Fires once for each failed payment attempt on an open invoice, and again for each failed retry.

actions.label: Create a customer
actions.description: Create a customer. Identical inputs within 24 hours return the first customer rather than a second one.

actions.label: Get a customer
actions.description: Read a customer by id. A deleted customer comes back with deleted true and little else.

actions.label: List recent charges
actions.description: The most recent charges, newest first. Amounts are integers in the smallest currency unit.

actions.label: Refund a payment
actions.description: Refund a payment intent or charge, in full or for an amount in the smallest currency unit. Identical inputs within 24 hours return the first refund.

actions.label: Get the account balance
actions.description: The current balance of the account the key belongs to, in the smallest currency unit per currency.

actions.label: List customers
actions.description: Customers newest first, optionally only those with one exact email address.

env.name: STRIPE_API_KEY
env.description: Leave empty to borrow the Stripe CLI login. A restricted key with read access to customers, charges, invoices and payment intents plus write access to customers and refunds is enough.

env.name: STRIPE_LIVE_MODE
env.description: true borrows the live key from the CLI profile instead of the test one. A pasted key carries its own mode.

env.name: STRIPE_PROJECT
env.description: The stripe --project-name profile to borrow from. Blank for the default profile.

env.name: STRIPE_CUSTOMER
env.description: Only this customer’s invoices, for the two invoice triggers. Blank for every customer.

env.name: STRIPE_LOOKBACK_MINUTES
env.description: How far before the watermark the payment and paid-invoice polls re-read, to catch an intent or invoice that succeeded a while after it was created.

env.name: STRIPE_FAILED_LOOKBACK_MINUTES
env.description: How far before now the failed-invoice poll reads open invoices. A day by default, because retries are days apart.

connectors.name: Telegram
connectors.description: Trigger workflows from Telegram messages, and send, reply or edit from a step.
connectors.auth: Paste a bot token from @BotFather. There is no Telegram CLI to sign in with, and Telegram's OAuth grants only outbound messaging, never reads.

triggers.label: A message arrives
triggers.description: Fires for each new or edited message the bot can see. Telegram deletes unread updates after 24 hours and has no history endpoint, so this sees nothing sent before the connection was made.

actions.label: Send a message
actions.description: Post a message to a chat the bot is in.

actions.label: Reply to a message
actions.description: Post a message as a reply, so it threads under the original.

actions.label: Edit a message
actions.description: Replace the text of a message this bot sent.

env.name: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN
env.description: Create a bot with @BotFather in Telegram and paste the token it gives you. One token can only be read by one connection — a second one steals this one’s messages.

env.name: TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID
env.description: Numeric chat id, or @username for a public channel. Blank watches every chat the bot is in.

env.name: TELEGRAM_UPDATE_TYPES
env.description: Comma-separated. One or more of message, edited_message, channel_post, edited_channel_post.

env.name: TELEGRAM_POLL_TIMEOUT
env.description: How long Telegram may hold the connection open waiting for a message. 0 is short polling, which Telegram documents as being for testing only.

env.name: TELEGRAM_LIMIT
env.description: 1 to 100. Anything left over is read by the next poll.

connectors.name: Trello
connectors.description: Trigger workflows from cards created, moved, commented on or due soon on a Trello board, and create, update, move, comment on, label, archive, read and search cards from a step.
connectors.auth: Paste a Power-Up API key from trello.com/power-ups/admin and the member token its authorization page grants for read and write. There is no Trello CLI to sign in with.

triggers.label: A card is created
triggers.description: Fires once for each card created on the board since the last poll, oldest first.

triggers.label: A card moves to another list
triggers.description: Fires once for each card moved between lists on the board, with the list before and after. Set a destination list to fire only on arrivals there.

triggers.label: A comment is added
triggers.description: Fires once for each comment added to a card on the board since the last poll.

triggers.label: A card is due soon
triggers.description: Fires once per due date for each open card on the board whose due date falls within the configured hours and is not marked complete. A changed due date fires again.

actions.label: Create a card
actions.description: Add a card to a list.

actions.label: Update a card
actions.description: Change the name, description, due date, due-complete flag or archived state of a card; only the inputs given are sent.

actions.label: Move a card
actions.description: Move a card to a list, optionally at a position or onto another board.

actions.label: Add a comment
actions.description: Comment on a card.

actions.label: Add a label to a card
actions.description: Put a label on a card. A label already on the card is reported as present rather than as a failure.

actions.label: Archive a card
actions.description: Archive a card. A second call leaves it archived.

actions.label: Get a card
actions.description: Read one card with its list and board.

actions.label: List boards
actions.description: The boards the token’s member belongs to, open ones by default.

actions.label: List lists on a board
actions.description: The lists of a board, open ones by default.

actions.label: List cards in a list
actions.description: The open cards of a list.

actions.label: Search cards
actions.description: Find cards matching a query across the member’s boards or the given ones.

env.name: TRELLO_API_KEY
env.description: The Power-Up API key: create a Power-Up at https://trello.com/power-ups/admin, open its API Key tab and generate a key.

env.name: TRELLO_TOKEN
env.description: The member token the API key’s Token link grants: approve read and write access with expiration never, then copy the token shown.

env.name: TRELLO_BOARD_ID
env.description: The board the triggers watch, by id or by the short link from its URL (trello.com/b/<shortLink>/…).

env.name: TRELLO_TO_LIST_ID
env.description: For the card-moved trigger: only fire when a card lands in this list. Blank fires on every move.

env.name: TRELLO_WITHIN_HOURS
env.description: For the card-due-soon trigger: how many hours ahead a due date must fall to fire.

connectors.name: X
connectors.description: Trigger workflows from new mentions or posts matching a search on X, and create, reply to, delete, read and search posts from a step.
connectors.auth: Paste the four OAuth 1.0a credentials of an X developer app with Read and Write permission; there is no X CLI to borrow a login from.

triggers.label: New mention
triggers.description: A post mentions the connected account. Polls the mentions timeline with since_id; a burst above 100 mentions between polls loses the oldest. Access: 300 requests per 15 minutes per user, billed per post read (an Owned Read when the account owns the app). Metered per request and per post read; see the README for the price and the rate limit of each call.

triggers.label: New search result
triggers.description: A post from the last 7 days matches the search query with since_id; a burst above 100 matches between polls loses the oldest. Access: 300 requests per 15 minutes per user, billed per post returned; recent search is the read that used to need a paid tier. Metered per request and per post read; see the README for the price and the rate limit of each call.

actions.label: Create post
actions.description: Publish a post of up to 280 characters, optionally as a reply or a quote. Needs Read and Write permission.

actions.label: Reply to post
actions.description: Reply to a post with up to 280 characters. Needs Read and Write permission.

actions.label: Delete post
actions.description: Delete one of the connected account's own posts. Needs Read and Write permission.

actions.label: Get me
actions.description: The connected account. Access: 75 requests per 15 minutes per user, one user read. Metered per request and per post read; see the README for the price and the rate limit of each call.

actions.label: Get post
actions.description: A post by id with its author and public metrics. Access: 900 requests per 15 minutes per user, one post read plus one user read. Metered per request and per post read; see the README for the price and the rate limit of each call.

actions.label: Get user by username
actions.description: A user by handle. Access: 900 requests per 15 minutes per user, one user read. Metered per request and per post read; see the README for the price and the rate limit of each call.

actions.label: Search recent posts
actions.description: Posts from the last 7 days matching a query, newest first. Access: 300 requests per 15 minutes per user, billed per post returned; this is the read that used to need a paid tier. Metered per request and per post read; see the README for the price and the rate limit of each call.

env.name: X_API_KEY
env.description: The app's API Key (OAuth 1.0a consumer key).

env.name: X_API_SECRET
env.description: The app's API Key Secret (consumer secret).

env.name: X_ACCESS_TOKEN
env.description: The Access Token generated for your own account under Keys and tokens.

env.name: X_ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET
env.description: The Access Token Secret shown with the access token.

env.name: X_SEARCH_QUERY
env.description: Recent-search query the "new search result" trigger polls, such as `from:xdevelopers -is:retweet`.

templates.name: Morning digest
templates.description: Every weekday morning, gather what changed overnight and have an agent write it up.

config.prompt:
Write a short digest of these commits for the team:

{{steps.execute-script.output}}

templates.name: Triage new tasks
templates.description: When a task is created, have an agent read it and say what it will take.

templates.name: Webhook to report
templates.description: Take a request from another system, look at what it says, and post the ones that matter on somewhere else.
